previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and bilateral lower extremity amputations was readmitted two days after discharge due to a productive cough, shortness of breath, and poor oral intake. She had recently completed treatment for Staphylococcus epidermidis bacteremia and was still on vancomycin. Chest X-ray revealed right upper and possibly right lower lobe pneumonia, consistent with healthcare-associated pneumonia. She was treated with intravenous Zosyn, which was later transitioned to oral levofloxacin. Her white blood cell count improved from 19.1 to 9.2 within two days, and she became afebrile with improved respiratory status. A catheter exit site swab showed sparse Candida albicans, deemed likely contamination; however, a two-week course of fluconazole was initiated as a precaution. Blood cultures remained negative, and she tolerated oral intake by discharge. She was discharged home with services to complete antibiotics and antifungal therapy, continue vancomycin with dialysis, and follow up with her care team.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your stay at ___. 
You were admitted to the medical ICU for concern of 
gastrointestinal bleeding. You were given blood in the ICU, and 
you were stabilized. You were then transferred to the regular 
medicine floor, where you were found to have an infected HD 
catheter. We removed the infected line and tried to put another 
line in your right neck, but were unable to do so because a 
large vein was blocked. Instead, we put in a temporary HD 
catheter in the groin. You were treated for the line infection 
with anti-fungal medications because we found fungus growing at 
the site. When the infection cleared, we placed another 
permanent HD catheter in your left neck, which will be used for 
dialysis in the future. We removed the temporary catheter in 
your groin.

You had a fever after the temporary HD line was placed in your 
groin. The fever was concerning for a bacterial infection, so we 
treated you with antibiotics. You had no further fevers, and you 
do not need to take antibiotics when you leave the hospital.

While here, you were seen by gastroenterology who initally 
recommended a colonoscopy and EGD. However, because we were 
unable to get a peripheral IV in your vein, we were unable to do 
the colonoscopy and EGD.  Fortunately, your red blood cells were 
stable, and there was no evidence of active bleeding after you 
were transfused blood. Please follow up with Dr. ___ at the 
appointment listed below. He will help connect you with a 
gastroenterologist to evaluate whether colonoscopy and EGD are 
still necessary. 

In addition, please follow up with ___ at the ___ 
___ at the appointment listed below. Your blood 
sugars were sometimes very low and sometimes very high while you 
were here, and you require close follow up.

You continued to get dialysis while you were here. Please resume 
dialysis at your outpatient facility according to your usual 
schedule. 

Thank you for allowing us to take part in your care.

FINDINGS:  There is a low-density left pleural effusion causing secondary

lower lobe, suggesting chronic infection.  Again seen are ill-defined
parenchymal opacities and bronchiectasis in the right upper lobe, suggestive
of chronic infection.  There is segmental atelectasis at the right lung base
(3:44).  The airways are patent to the subsegmental level. Anterior bowing of
the posterior tracheal wall is noted consitent with tracheomalacia.

The thyroid gland is normal.  There is no axillary or supraclavicular
lymphadenopathy.  Left-sided IJ hemodialysis catheter terminates in the
cavoatrial junction.  Coronary artery calcifications are again noted.  The
heart is normal in size.  There are scattered prominent lymph nodes in the
upper mediastinum, but unchanged from prior CT.

Though not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, the visualized portions
of the liver, spleen, and adrenals are normal.  Again seen are perifissural
nodules (3:23).

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  Defects in the left seventh rib is presumably from prior
thoracotomy, unchanged.  There is no lytic or blastic lesion suspicious for
malignancy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Small left pleural effusion with coursing along the parietal pleura. 
Secondary empyema cannot be excluded by imaging.
2.  Multiple areas of bronchiectasis, particularly in the right upper and left
lower lobes, suggesting chronic infection.
3.  Trachea changes consistent with tracheomalacia.
4.  Coronary artery disease.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with infected HD catheter, in need for removal.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ (fellow) and Dr. ___ (attending)
performed the procedure.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  The indwelling left-sided tunneled HD catheter was prepped
and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Lidocaine was then injected into the
tunnel.  The sutures were cut, and the catheter could be easily withdrawn. 
Pressure was then applied to the venotomy site for 10 minutes, and a soft
dressing applied.

IMPRESSION:  Successful removal of left-sided tunneled hemodialysis line.

INDICATION:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease and infected left
tunneled catheter which was removed one day prior.  Please place new dialysis
access.

COMPARISONS:  None.

PROCEDURE:  Temporary dialysis catheter placement in the right femoral vein.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ (radiology resident) and Dr. ___
___ attending) performed the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Local anesthesia was provided using 1% lidocaine to the dermis. 
Moderate conscious sedation was performed with 50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of
Versed by a radiology nurse.  The patient's hemodynamic parameters were
monitored throughout the procedure.

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the risks, benefits, and possible complications of the procedure. 
The patient was transported to the angiography suite and placed in the supine
position on the imaging table.  The right internal jugular vein was evaluated
using ultrasound.  It was found to be occluded and unsuitable for a catheter
placement. The renal fellow, Dr. ___ was contacted and a recommendation was
made to place a temporary access in the groin. The right groin was evaluated
by ultrasound and the right femoral vein was patent.

The right groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed as per the ___ protocol.  After
anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, micropuncture needle was
inserted into the right femoral vein under ultrasound guidance.  A 0.018
Nitinol wire was advanced into the inferior vena cava.  After additional local
anesthetic was administered, small ___ was made in the sheets.  A
micropuncture needle was then removed over the wire.  The incision site was
dilated with sequential dilators.  A temporary hemodialysis catheter was
advanced over the wire.  Under fluoroscopic guidance, catheter tip was in the
appropriate position in the inferior vena cava, just beyond the bifurcation of
the iliac veins.  Both lumens withdrew blood and flushed easily.  The catheter
was secured with ___ silk sutures.  A sterile dressing was applied and dated.

Noted during fluoroscopic evaluation was an IVC filter.  This precluded
placement of a tunneled dialysis catheter in the groin.  Also, identified was
a catheter overlying the lower abdomen extending through the right abdominal
wall, consistent with the patient's peritoneal dialysis catheter.

Total fluoroscopic time was 2.6 minutes with a DLP of 4 mGy.

IMPRESSION:
Successful placement of a temporary hemodialysis catheter through the right
femoral vein approach.  The tip is located in the inferior vena cava.  The
catheter is ready for use.

INDICATION:  ___ female with a temporary dialysis in the right groin,
please place left jugular tunneled dialysis line.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ (attending), Dr. ___ and Dr.
___.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
fentanyl and Versed throughout the total in-service time of 25 minutes, during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.

Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine and 1% lidocaine with
epinephrine into the subcutaneous tissues.

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient, after
explaining the risks, benefits, alternatives and indications of the procedure.
The patient was transported to the angiographic suite and placed supine on the
imaging table.  The left neck was prepped and draped in usual sterile fashion.
A preprocedural timeout and huddle was performed per ___ protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, a micropuncture needle
was inserted into a left external jugular vein collateral under ultrasound
guidance.  Hard copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018
nitinol wire was advanced into the superior vena cava.  After additional
anesthesia, a small ___ was made in the skin.  The micropuncture needle was
exchanged with a micropuncture sheath and the inner cannula and nitinol wire
were removed.  A 0.035 J-wire was advanced into the right atrium and
appropriate measurements were made.  The wire was then advanced into the IVC,
just superior to an IVC filter.

Attention was then turned to the creation of a subcutaneous tunnel.  After
additional local anesthesia was provided, a 1-cm skin incision was made.  A 10
___ tunneled catheter was passed from the incision to the venotomy site
with the aid of a metal tunneling device.  The venotomy tract was dilated with
7 and 9 ___ dilators and peel-away sheath was passed over the wire.  The
wire and inner cannula were removed and a 23-cm tip-to-cuff dialysis catheter
was advanced into the right atrium.  The position was confirmed with
fluoroscopy.  Both lumens withdrew blood and flushed easily.  The catheter was
secured using ___ silk sutures and the venotomy site was closed with a ___
Vicryl subcuticular stitch.  Dry sterile dressings were applied.  There were
no immediate post-procedure complications and the patient tolerated the
procedure well.

IMPRESSION:  Successful placement of a left external jugular vein 23-cm
tip-to-cuff tunneled hemodialysis catheter with its tip located in the right
atrium.  The catheter is ready to use.
